1.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State-respondents and Sri V.C. Upadhayay holding brief of learned counsel for the respondent No.2 - U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad.

2. The petitioners claim to be bona-fide purchasers have approached to this court assailing the validity of the impugned order dated 23.12.2022 passed by the respondent No.2 under Section 83 of U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad Adhiniyam, 1965.

sentences.text: 1 3. Sri V.C. Upadhayay holding brief of learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has raised an objection regarding maintainability of the writ petition on three-fold submissions.

Firstly, the property in question has been acquired under the Madhola Land Development and Homestead Scheme Block-2 by the respondent No.2, which has been notified under Section 28 of U.P. Avas Vikas Parishad Adhiniyam, 1965 (in short 'the Act, 1965') on 15.02.20003 and under Section 32 on 22.05.2010.

entities.text: Madhola Land Development and Homestead Scheme Block-2 by
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He submits that as per case set up by the petitioners themselves, the property in question had been purchased on 27.07.2010.
He submits that admittedly after notification under Section 28, any transfer of the property is impermissible.
Section 28 is pari materia of Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
He submits that as the property in question vests in Avas Evam Vikas Parishad, the petitioners cannot challenge the acquisition proceeding.

Secondly, it is pressed that the impugned order of demolition had been passed way back on 23.12.2022, the present writ petition is liable to be dismissed on the ground of delay and laches as no plausible reason has been given while instituting the present proceeding.

Lastly, he submits that despite the opportunity of hearing was provided to the petitioners to provide their side, no satisfactory response had been filed by them, therefore, on this score also, no indulgence is required in the matter.
4. We have occasion to peruse the record and the facts.

It is not in dispute that the property in question belongs to the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad and notifications under Sections 28 and 32 of the Act, 1965 were carried and admittedly the property was transferred on a later date.

Needless to say that in case the petitioners are bona fide purchasers, they may approach for compensation as per the law laid down by the Apex Court in Government of NCT of Delhi Vs. Manav Dharam Trust and others, (2017) 6 SCC 751.
5.

entities.text: Government of NCT of Delhi Vs. Manav Dharam Trust and others, (2017) 6 SCC 751
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With the aforesaid observations, the present writ petition is disposed of.
